name: Běhej lesy Bílá
location: Bílá, Beskydy, Moravian-Silesian Region, Czech Republic
description: Běhej lesy Bílá is a mountain trail race held in the beautiful Beskydy Protected Landscape Area. The race offers several routes, including short and long options, with the long ČSOB 20 km route included in the international UTMB Index. Runners can take the cable car to the summit and look forward to special speed sections, the Conti Speed Section and Generali Investments Finish, which add extra competitive challenges and rewards. The race is suitable for all mountain trail running enthusiasts who want to experience the beauty of the Beskydy Mountains while competing on well-marked routes.
course_highlights: Routes run through the Beskydy Protected Landscape Area, with respect for nature and a ban on leaving marked trails
Conti Speed Section – a timed 200-metre speed section on the Nova 11 km and ČSOB 20 km routes
Generali Investments Finish – an extended 500 m finishing straight with a timed section and performance analysis
additional: The race is part of the UTMB Index Races, with international ranking points. A cable car to the summit of the Bílá ski resort is available. At the finish, there is an extended 500 m straight with the timed Generali Investments Finish section, where the fastest men and women are announced and receive a Craft technical running shirt. Trail routes of varying lengths, a cable-car ride to the summit, speed sections, a charity race, respect for the Beskydy Protected Landscape Area, and GPX routes available for download.

name: Zlatá stezka
location: Stožec, Šumava, Jihočeský kraj, Czech Republic
description: The Golden Trail is a historic international hiking route connecting Bohemia with the Danube region, passing through the beautiful landscapes of the Šumava and Bavarian Forests. The 631 km route offers a unique experience by linking up with Germany’s Golden Trail and passing through several national parks and nature reserves. Hikers can discover historic towns, castles, observation towers and cultural landmarks along the trail, which is equipped with information boards and rest areas. The Golden Trail is ideal for hiking and exploring the natural and historical attractions of the South Bohemian and Plzeň regions.
course_highlights: The route passes through Šumava National Park and the Bavarian Forest, the largest forested areas in Central Europe
The historic towns of Prachatice, Vimperk and Kašperské Hory, with cultural landmarks and museums
A cross-border connection with Germany’s Golden Trail, with 13 border-crossing points
additional: The route is marked with the Golden Trail logo and equipped with information boards and rest areas. It offers various stages of differing difficulty and length. Cultural and natural attractions near the route include the Volary Museum, Libín Lookout Tower, and historic landmarks such as Hus Castle and Vimperk Castle. The route offers different distances and difficulty levels, including an ultra challenge and sports challenges, with the option to register in advance. The event is suitable for runners, cyclists and hikers who want to explore the region actively and with respect for nature.

name: 2 míle s úsměvem Zlín - srpen
description: The 2-Mile Run in Zlín-Příluky is an open 3.2 km race for all ages and running abilities, from beginners to experienced runners. The course runs mostly among gardens in the Příluky-Zlín industrial zone and consists of just under two laps of a precisely measured asphalt loop. The race also includes an 800-metre children’s course. Every participant can enjoy a warm cinnamon pancake at the finish. The race takes place on the first Saturday of every month, with registration from 8:15 to 8:55 and the start at 9:00.
course_highlights: The course runs mostly among gardens in the Příluky-Zlín industrial zone
A precisely measured asphalt loop, just under two laps long (3.2 km)
The children’s course is 800 metres long
additional: Registration takes place in front of the Madal Bal company building. Categories are divided into men and women aged 13 to 127, and children up to 12 years old. Every runner is timed, and the top three in each category receive small prizes. Recommended ways to get to the start are by bicycle, on foot, by car, on roller skates, or by trolleybus No. 11 (Průmyslová zóna stop). The course is 3.2 km long with an asphalt surface; the children’s course is 800 m. The run is for all age groups, including children up to 12 years old. It takes place on the first Saturday of every month, with registration from 8:15 to 8:55 and the starting gun at 9:00.

name: Běh na Kamenný stůl
location: Rataje nad Sázavou, Central Bohemian Region, Czech Republic
description: The Run to the Stone Table is a traditional running race held in Rataje nad Sázavou, celebrating its 10th anniversary this year. The race offers a challenging and beautiful course from the castle courtyard to the Stone Table landmark, with varied surfaces and hilly terrain. It is open to professional runners, amateurs, and families with children, for whom shorter routes are available. The race is part of the Run the Castles series, which brings together running events at attractive castle locations.
course_highlights: The course leads to the Stone Table landmark and includes varied surfaces: cobblestones, asphalt, and paved and unpaved forest paths
Hilly terrain, with part of the course running through the forest and along field paths
Start and finish directly in the courtyard of the castle in Rataje nad Sázavou
additional: Race bibs with a chip and name, water, a biscuit, promotional materials, and a castle admission ticket. Children receive a voucher for ice cream and adults a voucher for a sausage. Fruit, cakes, and refreshments are available at the event facilities. Parking is available at the sports field on Zámecká Street and at other nearby locations. Results are announced after participants finish each route. Registration includes a race pack, refreshments, and castle admission; races take place under normal traffic conditions.

name: 2 míle s úsměvem Praha - srpen
location: Stromovka Park, Praha 7, Prague, Czech Republic
description: The 2-mile run in Prague’s Stromovka Park is an open 3.2 km race for all ages and running levels, including children under 12, who run 1.6 km. The race is friendly and focused on the joy of running, whether you want to improve your personal best or simply enjoy a pleasant run in beautiful surroundings. The course follows the park’s paved paths; adults run two laps and children one. At the finish, everyone is rewarded with a warm cinnamon pancake.
course_highlights: The course follows the paved paths of Stromovka Park
Adults run 2 laps (3.2 km); children under 12 run 1 lap (1.6 km)
The race takes place in the beautiful surroundings of Královská obora–Stromovka Park
additional: Registration takes place at the Bruselská brána area from 8:15 to 8:45, with online pre-registration available for faster check-in. Categories are divided by age and gender; results are adjusted using an age coefficient and count toward the year-long Lívancový pohár. Recommended ways to get there are by bicycle, on foot, on roller skates, or by tram (Výstaviště stop). Changing and bag-drop tents, a mobile valuables-storage facility, and toilet cubicles are available. Parking is recommended near the bridge to Císařský ostrov on Za elektrárnou Street. The race takes place in Stromovka Park, starts at 9:07, and registration is open from 8:15 to 8:45. Online registration is available; there are categories for different age groups, parking near the bridge to Císařský ostrov, changing facilities, and toilets. The race is held regularly on the first Saturday of each month.

name: Mšecká sedmička
organizer: Městys Mšec a TJ Sokol Mšec
description: Mšecká sedmička is a traditional running race held in Mšec, in the Central Bohemian Region. The race is 7 km long and follows forest and field paths, offering runners a pleasant natural setting. It starts at the TJ Sokol Mšec football field and is suitable for the general public. It is organized by the Municipality of Mšec and TJ Sokol Mšec, who provide a friendly atmosphere and quality organization.
course_highlights: 7 km course
Forest and field paths
Start and finish at the TJ Sokol Mšec football field
additional: The race is organized by the Municipality of Mšec and TJ Sokol Mšec. It is a mixed-type race on forest and field paths. It starts at the TJ Sokol Mšec football field. The course includes forest and field paths; registration requirements are not specified.

name: Libeř - Radlík
description: Libeř - Radlík is a 2.47 km uphill race with 170 m of elevation gain, part of the Běhy do kopců v Praze a okolí series. The route is not entirely uphill: it includes several flat sections and one downhill, adding interest and variety to the race. The atmosphere is friendly, and the entry fee is symbolic, with generous prizes for the winners from Botanicus. The race is suitable for runners looking for a challenge on hilly terrain near Prague.
course_highlights: 2.47 km route with 170 m of elevation gain
The route includes flat sections and one downhill
Part of the Běhy do kopců v Praze a okolí series
additional: The entry fee is symbolic, and the winners receive generous prizes from Botanicus. The route follows wide, partly gravel roads, which some runners mention in comments as a drawback compared with forest trails. The race has a friendly atmosphere despite somewhat punk-rock conditions. The route is not entirely uphill, with a few flat sections and one downhill; it follows wide, partly gravel roads; part of the Běhy do kopců series.

name: Trail Running Cup - Krkonošská padesátka
description: The Krkonoše 50 is a traditional trail race held in the picturesque surroundings of Špindlerův Mlýn in the Krkonoše Mountains. The race offers a challenging 50 km course with 1,784 metres of elevation gain, following marked paths and mountain trails. The start is at the Svatý Petr resort, and participants can use the central car park in Špindlerův Mlýn. The race is limited to 300 starters. Overall male and female winners are announced, along with winners in ten age categories for both men and women.
course_highlights: 50 km course with 1,784 m of elevation gain
The route follows marked paths and mountain trails in the Krkonoše Mountains
Checkpoints at 13, 18, 27, 33 and 39 km, and at the finish
additional: The race starts at the Svatý Petr resort in Špindlerův Mlýn. Parking is available at the central car park in Špindlerův Mlýn. A mobile phone is mandatory for all starters and must be working and fully charged. Littering outside aid stations is strictly prohibited. Switching from the long route to the shorter one is possible after notifying the checkpoint at Svatý Petr – Hotel Horal. The route is marked with black arrows on a yellow background only at junctions and turns. The participant limit is 300 runners. The race is open to men and women, registration is online, and race day is 1 August 2026.

name: HTV-SPARDA-Rheinuferlauf, 46. Int. Volkslauf mit HM
description: The HTV-SPARDA-Rheinuferlauf in Duisburg is a traditional road race with a flat course along the Rhine. On 25 July 2026, events will be held over 5 km, 7.5 km walking, 10 km and the half marathon (21.1 km). The flat course makes the race appealing to runners of all abilities. All events share the same finish line, and the event offers a pleasant atmosphere for recreational and competitive runners.
course_highlights: Flat course along the Rhine
Events over 5 km, 7.5 km walking, 10 km and the half marathon
All events finish at the same location
additional: Start times: 7.5 km walking at 15:00, 5 km run at 16:50, 10 km run at 17:40, half marathon at 17:30. All events take place on a flat course. Results will be published on the RUNME results page. The event takes place on 25 July 2026 and offers start times for various events. Results will be available shortly after the races finish. The event is particularly appealing in good weather.

name: Sechs-Std.-Lauf am Förderturm Bönen
location: Ehemaliges Zechengelände, Bönen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Six-Hour Run at the Bönen Headframe is a unique ultrarunning event held on an officially measured loop course at a former colliery site. The course is traffic-free, gently undulating, and consists of asphalt and compact gravel. The event offers comprehensive refreshments, including vegan options, and professional lap counting via race result. With a minimum age of 20, the run is aimed at experienced ultrarunners who want to test their endurance in a friendly, well-organized atmosphere.
course_highlights: Loop course at a former colliery site, traffic-free
Lap length: 1,340 m; surface: asphalt and compact gravel
Officially measured course with gentle undulations
additional: Race bib pickup on event day from 07:00 to 08:30. Showers and changing facilities are available at the nearby Goethe Sports Hall and in the Förderturm Shaft Hall (not supervised; no liability is accepted). A variety of food and drinks, including vegan options, will be provided before and during the run. Laps are counted electronically via race result, with measurement of the remaining distance. First aid is provided by the German Red Cross local branch in Bönen (DRK-Ortsverein Bönen e.V.). Awards ceremony at approximately 16:00. Minimum age: 20. Maximum 200 participants; on-site registration is possible for a €10 fee. Loop course at a former colliery site, vegan refreshments, race bib pickup 07:00–08:30, minimum age 20.

name: Die 10 Kilometer von Dürwiß
price_range: kostenlos, Anmeldung online oder vor Ort gegen Gebühr
description: The 10 km von Dürwiß is a traditional road race held annually on the first Saturday in August by SV Germania Dürwiß e.V. More than 500 runners from Germany and abroad take part, with winning times usually around 30 minutes. The flat, officially measured 2 km asphalt loop runs through the town center of Dürwiß and is completely closed to traffic on race day. What makes this cult race special are the many spectators and lively street parties along the course, with music and decorations creating a unique atmosphere. The event wraps up with an after-run party featuring DJ Steve and a wide selection of refreshments.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2 km asphalt loop through the town center of Dürwiß
Five laps for the 10 km main race, on streets completely closed to traffic
Lively street parties with music and decorations along the course
additional: In addition to the 10 km main race, there is a 4,000 m fun run, children’s and youth races from 200 m to 1,000 m, and a 10 km inline skating race with different lap formats depending on age group. The course is completely closed to road traffic on race day, and parking along the route is strictly prohibited. The event wraps up with an after-run party featuring DJ Steve and extensive refreshments. Course back to 10 km, inline skating and children’s races, street parties, after-run party, music, sponsor prizes

name: 18. Ottonenlauf
description: The Ottonenlauf is a scenic race in the Harz Mountains, bringing runners from three different villages to a shared finish in the UNESCO World Heritage City of Quedlinburg. The 21.1 km, 42.2 km and 69 km distances start in Stiege, Alexisbad and Meisdorf, respectively. The route runs mainly along forest and woodland paths through the Selke Valley, with shaded forests, rural sections and moderate climbs that call for a good pace. Walking and Nordic walking options are also available, making the event accessible to a wide range of participants. Electronic timing and finisher medals round out the event.
course_highlights: Scenic trail race along the Selketal-Stieg
Forest and woodland paths with shaded sections
Moderate climbs, with 809 m of ascent and more than 1,000 m of descent on the long course
additional: Three starting points for different distances, all finishing in Quedlinburg. Electronic timing and medals for all finishers. Typical August weather: approx. 25 °C and mostly sunny. Trail-style race with multiple distances, including walking options; course not officially measured; medals for all finishers; online registration; route through quiet Harz forest paths.

name: 24. Hella Marathon Nacht
description: The hella marathon nacht rostock is an atmospheric sunset run set against the picturesque backdrop of the Haedgehalbinsel in Rostock’s city harbour. The event offers races over the marathon, half marathon, Rostocker 7 km and a schoolchildren’s race. All start at dusk and finish beneath bright lights. The route passes through the Warnow Tunnel and IGA Park, among other places, and is closed to traffic. The event combines a sporting challenge with northern German hospitality and a holiday atmosphere.
course_highlights: The marathon route runs along the Warnow and through the Warnow Tunnel
The half marathon passes through IGA Park and runs along the Warnow to the city harbour
The Rostocker 7 km is a loop around the city harbour
additional: Start times: schoolchildren’s race 17:00, marathon 18:00, Rostocker 7 km 19:07. Finish closes at 23:30. Start and finish at the Haedgehalbinsel, Rostock city harbour. A technical shirt can be pre-ordered (€28, until 21.07.2026 only; collection only during event weekend). Race-pack collection on 31.07.2026 and 01.08.2026 on site. The event takes place in Rostock, with the start and finish on the Haedgehalbinsel at Rostock city harbour. It is known for its festive atmosphere, medals and professional timing. The routes run along the Warnow and through the Warnow Tunnel and IGA Park.

name: 5. TCW Backyard Ultra
description: The TCW Backyard Ultra in Wölfersheim is a unique running event focused on camaraderie and endurance. Runners start on the hour and must complete a 6.706 km loop within one hour. The race continues until only one runner remains, who is declared the winner. The event is known for its friendly atmosphere and supportive community, welcoming runners of all abilities.
course_highlights: 6.706 km loop on the tennis club grounds and adjoining field and farm tracks
Starts on the hour, with a maximum of one hour to complete each loop
Night running with headlamps between 21:00 and 6:00
additional: The race is an officially listed Backyard Ultra event and a potential qualifying race for the individual and team World Championships. Starts are announced acoustically with whistle signals and a bell. There is no time limit; the winner is the last runner remaining who completes one more loop than everyone else. Personal assistance on the course is not permitted, but participants may support one another. Trekking poles and artificial aids are prohibited. Participation is limited, so early registration is required; the event follows the Backyard Ultra format and regularly attracts over 400 applicants.

name: adidas Runners City Night
description: The adidas Runners City Night Berlin is a unique summer event that combines running and inline skating with a big party on the famous Kurfürstendamm. The event offers 5 km and 10 km courses for runners, as well as a 10 km inline skating course through the vibrant City West. Live bands, cheering zones and enthusiastic fans create an exhilarating atmosphere that makes the race an unforgettable experience. The finish at the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church, with its illuminated finish arch, is the perfect finale to this sporting night.
course_highlights: Course through City West and along Kurfürstendamm
Live bands and cheering points, especially at the adidas Cheering Zone at Adenauerplatz
Start and finish at the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
additional: Start times: 5 km run at 19:00, 10 km run at 20:00. Timing is recorded using a transponder on the back of the race bib. The 5 km run has a turnaround point; the 10 km run follows a star-shaped route with several passes by the adidas Cheering Zone. Eligibility: born in 2016 or earlier (5 km) or 2014 or earlier (10 km). Personalized medal engraving can be booked. Extras such as an event shirt and bag storage can be added during registration. The course runs along Kurfürstendamm and through Old West Berlin; the start is at sunset. Includes a medal with a lighting effect; medal engraving is optional. Online registration is available.

name: hella marathon nacht rostock
description: The hella marathon nacht rostock is an atmospheric sunset run along the Warnow, with maritime flair and Hanseatic hospitality. The event takes place in Rostock in August and offers races over the marathon, half marathon, Rostocker 7 and a children’s race. The start and finish are at Rostock’s city harbor, where runners set off at dusk and finish beneath bright lights. The course runs through the Warnow Tunnel and IGA Park, among other places, making for a unique running experience.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Rostock’s city harbor, with maritime flair
The course passes through the nearly 800 m-long Warnow Tunnel
Run through IGA Park with a picturesque sunset
additional: Start times: children’s race 17:00, marathon 18:00, Rostocker 7 approx. 19:07. Finish closes at 23:30. Marathon participants must pass the Warnow crossing checkpoint by 20:40. Pre-ordered technical shirts are available only during event weekend; no shipping by post. Race packet pickup at the event center on Haedge Peninsula, Rostock city harbor, on 31.07.2026 from 16:00–19:00 and on 01.08.2026 from 12:00–18:30. Event in August, dusk start, various race distances, finisher medals, certificates available immediately, optional event shirt, chip timing.

name: Hemfurth-Edersee-Abendlauf
description: The Hemfurth-Edersee Evening Run is a traditional late-summer event that brings runners of all ages together in the beautiful surroundings of Edertal-Hemfurth. In pleasant temperatures and as the sun sets, the focus is on the joy of running and a sense of community. Participants can look forward to refreshments, good music and a relaxed get-together at the finish. The run is organized on a voluntary basis by TSV 08 Hemfurth-Edersee e.V. and is a popular event for competitive runners, recreational joggers and families.
course_highlights: Run through the picturesque countryside around Lake Edersee
Evening start in pleasant temperatures
A shared running experience for all ages
additional: The Evening Run takes place annually in late summer, usually in early August. The event is organized on a voluntary basis. There are refreshments, music and a social get-together at the finish. Timing is done using special software that is used only once a year. The available pages do not provide explicit information about start times, price tiers or registration procedures. The event is part of the Waldeck-Frankenberg Running Cup. All finishers receive certificates, Bambini participants receive medals, and prizes are awarded to the top runners in the main categories. On-site registration is possible until 30 minutes before the start.

name: Mehrstetter Crosslauf
description: The Mehrstetten Cross-Country Run takes place on August 1, 2026, in Mehrstetten on the Swabian Alb. The event gives runners the opportunity to run in a well-maintained, natural setting. The municipality of Mehrstetten is known for its beautiful landscape and friendly atmosphere, making the cross-country run a special experience. The event is organized by the municipality of Mehrstetten and is a regular fixture in the local sports calendar.
course_highlights: Run through the natural landscape of the Swabian Alb
Well-maintained course in Mehrstetten
Event in a friendly and welcoming municipality
additional: Registration is via an online form on the municipal website. The municipality of Mehrstetten is the organizer and provides well-maintained facilities. The municipality’s contact form can be used to get in touch. Event is part of the SauHeld-Cup 2026. Runner information and a detailed course description are not available.

name: Pörndorfer Sommernachtslauf
description: The 15th Pörndorfer Summer Night Run on 1 August 2026 in Aldersbach is a running event with a family-friendly atmosphere and a genuine competitive spirit. It offers suitable challenges for all age groups and ability levels, from the Bambini Run through the children’s and youth races to the main race. Nordic walking is also part of the program. The event combines sporting ambition with a communal summer atmosphere and attracts runners and spectators from the region.
course_highlights: Races for all age groups, from Bambini to youth and the main race
Summer scenery and golden evening light
Nordic walking as a relaxed, inclusive discipline
additional: Registration is open until 24 July 2026 at 23:00. The venue is the DJK Pörndorf sports grounds, Sportplatzstr., 94501 Aldersbach. The event is organized by the DJK Pörndorf sports club. Various race distances, children’s and youth races, Nordic walking, registration until 24 July 2026

name: Schwindegger Schlosslauf
description: The Schwindegg Castle Run is an annual sporting event in the idyllic community of Schwindegg. Participants run along scenic paths and through forests, with views of Schwindegg Castle. There are various categories for all age groups, including children and teenagers. The event is also an opportunity to strengthen the community and support the sports club. Before and after the race, a summer festival with food, a drinks stand and a bar offers a cheerful atmosphere for celebrating and socialising.
course_highlights: Run along scenic paths and through forests
Impressive views of Schwindegg Castle
Various categories for children, teenagers and adults
additional: The race takes place as part of the Schwindegg Sports Club’s summer festival, which offers food and drinks before and after the race in a convivial atmosphere. There is a drinks stand and bar for runners and spectators. The event also includes a 0.5 km Bambini run at the school sports ground. Various categories, community spirit and a summer festival in scenic surroundings

name: SWE Halbmarathon Ettlingen
description: The SWE Ettlingen Half Marathon is a challenging and varied 21.1 km cross-country race connecting several Ettlingen districts at different elevations. The route starts in the picturesque Horbachpark and leads through wooded areas with distant views of the Black Forest before descending into the Rhine Plain and finishing at Horbachsee. Refreshment stations are provided every 3 km, and local residents offer refreshments and create an encouraging atmosphere. The race takes place on 1 August 2026 and is organised by SSV Ettlingen 1847 e. V., Lauftreff Ettlingen department.
course_highlights: A challenging 21.1 km cross-country race with elevation changes
Woodland sections with distant views of the Black Forest and the Palatinate Mountains
Finish at the scenic Horbachsee in the former State Garden Show grounds
additional: The start and finish are in Horbachpark, by the pavilion, Middelkerker Straße, 76275 Ettlingen. There are two wave starts, approximately 3 minutes apart, to ease congestion during the first kilometres. The field is limited to a maximum of 800 starters. Late entries are possible at the Albgauhalle on race weekend. All pre-registered participants receive a gift with their race number. The team with the most finishers is rewarded with two bottles of champagne. Timing is via a transponder in the race number, with net-time results. Terrain: paved paths, gravel paths, asphalt; registration deadline: 27.07.2026; maximum 800 participants; start times: 16:00 walkers, 17:00 runners; children’s and youth races are new for 2026.

name: Botaniczna Piątka Łódź edycja letnia
price_range: w formularzu zgłoszeniowym na edycje letnie
description: Botaniczna Piątka Łódź – Summer Edition is a cross-country race organized by running enthusiasts since 2014. The event takes place on scenic routes that showcase the aesthetic appeal of the locations. The organizers aim to popularize running and provide participants with a unique sporting and scenic experience. It’s a great opportunity to spend time actively and join a close-knit running community.
course_highlights: A cross-country race on scenic routes
The aesthetic appeal of the proposed locations
Organized since 2014, with an emphasis on popularizing running
additional: Registration for the main distance and children’s races in the Summer Edition has closed. The organizers run a newsletter to share updates. Trzymsie.pl is a partner of the autumn Botaniczna Piątka series. Scenic routes, cross-country races, locations in Łódź

name: 32. Bieg św. Dominika
description: The St. Dominic’s International Run is a prestigious running event held annually in Gdańsk since 1994 and an integral part of St. Dominic’s Fair. The race attracts over 1,200 participants and tens of thousands of spectators, offering a unique atmosphere in the city’s historic centre. The course runs through the picturesque streets of Gdańsk’s Old Town, and the event promotes a healthy lifestyle and social integration. The running festival features several races, including the 5 km Women’s Run, the 5 km Men’s Run and the Polish 10 km Championships.
course_highlights: A 1,412 m loop through central Gdańsk, starting and finishing by Neptune’s Fountain
The route passes along Długi Targ, Powroźnicza, Kotwiczników, Podwale Przedmiejskie and other streets
Cheering from more than 25,000 spectators along the course
additional: The course is a 1,412 m loop in central Gdańsk, allowing spectators to follow the competition closely. The event is accompanied by the varied programme of St. Dominic’s Fair, with concerts, shows and partner stands. The run promotes social integration, a healthy lifestyle and sport for people with disabilities as part of the “Chase St. Dominic” prologue. The event includes various race categories for women, men, elite runners and VIPs, with a wide range of age groups. Participants can support charitable causes through their entry fees, which go towards various social initiatives.

name: Arm Race Kamień
location: Cekow-Kolonia, Kamień County, West Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland
description: ARM Race Kamień is an extreme OCR obstacle race that welcomes both professionals and amateurs looking for an adrenaline rush. It is a challenge for whole families, including children, offering unusual entertainment and a chance to overcome personal weaknesses. The race is among Poland’s elite events of this kind and continues to grow, giving participants unforgettable experiences.
course_highlights: Extreme OCR obstacle race
Courses for different experience levels: PRO 10K, PRO 5K, OPEN 10K, OPEN 5K, FUN 5K, Pomarańczowy Wojownik
An event for families with children, amateurs, and professionals
additional: Distances: 5K and 10K; various formats; natural terrain; online registration

name: IX Rudzki Półmaraton Industrialny
organizer: RUDA Śląska i MOSiR Ruda Śląska
description: The 9th Ruda Industrial Half Marathon will take place on August 1 at 9:00 p.m. in Ruda Śląska. The 10.5 km course runs through the city center, showcasing the region’s industrial character and post-industrial landmarks such as Chebzie railway station, the Mikołaj Shaft, the Kaufhaus estate, and the blast furnace at Pokój Steelworks. In addition to the half marathon, an accompanying race of approximately 10 km is organized for people who do not feel able to run the full distance. The start and finish are at the athletics stadium on Czarnoleśna Street, which also houses the race office and organizational facilities.
course_highlights: A 10.5 km loop through the city center
Passes post-industrial landmarks: Chebzie railway station, the Mikołaj Shaft, and the Kaufhaus estate
Passes the only blast furnace in Silesia, at Pokój Steelworks
additional: The start and finish are at the athletics stadium on Czarnoleśna Street, which also houses the race office and facilities. An accompanying race of approximately 10 km is available for those not ready to run a half marathon. Registration takes place on the DO:ST:AR:TU platform. The course passes post-industrial landmarks; the start and finish are at the athletics stadium; registration is on the DO:ST:AR:TU platform; accompanying events include a 10 km race and Nordic walking; the half marathon is certified by the PZLA.

name: XI Czastarska Piątka
description: The 11th Czastary Five is an annual road race held in the Czastary municipality, attracting runners from various regions. The event combines sport and recreation and follows a 5-kilometer route through the municipality’s picturesque areas. The organizers provide a welcoming atmosphere and support for participants, promoting an active lifestyle and integration within the local community.
course_highlights: 5 km route
Road race through the picturesque areas of the Czastary municipality
Sport and recreation event
additional: Registration for the race opens on May 5, 2026; route details have not been provided in detail

name: Bieg z okazji 82. Rocznicy Wybuchu Powstania Warszawskiego
II Wielgomłyński Dycha
location: Wielgomłyny, Radomsko County, Łódź Voivodeship, Poland

name: Bear Foot Poľana
price_range: € 1 - € 40 (podľa vlny registrácie a dostupnosti na mieste)
description: BEAR FOOT POĽANA 2026 is a mountain race in the wild and unique Poľana Mountains, the highest and best-preserved volcano in Central Europe. The race offers two main courses: 24 km with 1,300+ metres of cumulative ascent and 10 km with 600+ metres of ascent. The course passes through popular hiking destinations such as Bystrô Waterfall, the Celtic hillfort of Kaľamárka and the summit of Predná Poľana, while runners enjoy the beauty of deep forests, mountain streams and pastures. The race is part of the Slovak Skyrunning Association league and is limited to 150 runners per course.
course_highlights: 24 km course with 1,300+ m of cumulative ascent, passing Bystrô Waterfall and the Celtic hillfort of Kaľamárka
10 km course with 600+ m of ascent, starting and finishing at Horský hotel Poľana
The course combines hiking trails, forest roads and mountain meadows
additional: Race check-in is open from 7:30 to 9:30; late registration is not possible. Bells or small bells must be used throughout the entire course. There are three refreshment stations at 4.4 km, 10 km and 15 km. The entry fee includes refreshments during and after the race, a unique race bib, a participant pack and timing. The limit is 150 runners per course. The race includes a 24 km course with more than 1,300 m of ascent, is part of the Slovak Skyrunning League, has limited registration and takes place on 1 August 2026.

name: Porubska 11-ka
description: Porúbska 11-ka is a running race held in the village of Porúbka in Bardejov District. It features gently rolling, hilly to flat terrain at an elevation of 196 m. The course passes through the Carpathian region, offering a combination of flat sections and hills, ideal for runners looking for an enjoyable run surrounded by nature. The race is organized by the municipality of Porúbka and is part of local sporting activities with a tradition and a strong community spirit. The event is suitable for the general public and promotes an active lifestyle in the region.
course_highlights: Gently rolling, hilly to flat terrain
Elevation: 196 m
The route passes through the Carpathian region
additional: The race takes place on August 1, 2026; registration is available via Google Forms; the routes run through the countryside around Porúbka; the event is supported by the local community and a passion for sport.

name: Island Gladiator Slovakia
description: Island Gladiator Slovakia is an OCR race that will test your strength, endurance and determination in Slovakia’s authentic natural environment. The course runs through meadows, forests, streams and hills, with various technical sections and obstacles such as walls, crawling, pulling, balancing and carrying weights. The race is open to men and women, beginners and experienced athletes, with a 3-hour time limit. Every participant receives an official T-shirt, a medal, a race pack and electronic timekeeping. Island Gladiator is not just a competition, but a challenge to overcome yourself and become a stronger gladiator.
course_highlights: The course runs through meadows, forests, streams and hills
Technical sections with obstacles such as walls, crawling, pulling, balancing and carrying weights
A 3-hour time limit to complete the course
additional: Every participant receives an official T-shirt, a unique medal, electronic timekeeping, a race pack with a surprise from the partners, refreshments and food at the finish or on the course. Failing to complete an obstacle means a penalty of 20 burpees or a penalty lap. Outside assistance is allowed only with the organizers’ consent. The race starts at 09:00 in timed waves. Registration is available through their website, and early-bird discounts are also available.

name: 2 míle s úsměvem Olomouc - srpen
description: The Olomouc 2-Mile Run is an open 2-mile (3.2 km) race for all ages and running abilities, from beginners to experienced runners. The event focuses on the joy of running and personal achievement, with everyone competing primarily against themselves. It is usually held in Smetana Gardens by the fountain, except for the June and August races, which take place by the river on U Dětského domova Street. The event also includes a cup competition, where results are adjusted using an age coefficient and points are accumulated throughout the year.
course_highlights: 2-mile (3.2 km) course; 600 m children’s race
The course usually runs through Smetana Gardens in Olomouc, by the fountain
The June and August races take place by the river on U Dětského domova Street
additional: Registration is from 9:30 to 10:00. The top three finishers in each category receive awards. Results are adjusted using an age coefficient, and points are accumulated in the cup competition for the period September 2025–August 2026. The event includes a 3.2 km asphalt course and a 600 m children’s race; registration is from 9:30 to 10:00; the event takes place on 2 August 2026.

name: Běžím Krušnohořím Moldava
location: Moldava, Krušné hory, Ústecký kraj, Czech Republic
description: Běžím Krušnohořím is a running and canicross series that takes you through the beauty of the Ore Mountains. The series includes 6 races in different locations, including Moldava, with routes for runners, canicross participants, children, and walkers. Each race offers a main running race of 6 to 9 km, an adventure route of 20 to 30 km navigated by map, a 5 to 8 km walk with checkpoints to find, and children’s races from 200 to 1600 metres. The series is suitable for the general public who want to explore the beauty of the Ore Mountains actively and through sport.
course_highlights: Main race: 6–9 km through the natural landscapes of the Ore Mountains
Adventure route: 20–30 km, navigated by map with orienteering elements
Children’s races and a 5–8 km walk with checkpoints to find
additional: The series includes 6 races in different locations across the Ore Mountains. The routes are suitable for runners, canicross participants, children, and walkers. Children’s races range from 200 to 1600 metres. The adventure routes are navigated by map, and the walking route includes finding checkpoints. The races are part of a series with an overall ranking and winners announced at the final race in Stříbrná; the event also includes races with dogs and children’s categories.

name: virtueller St.-Anna-Jedermannslauf
description: The virtual St. Anna Jedermannslauf in Amerdingen is a popular running event held annually in July. Participants can run the original courses of 10 km, 5.8 km jogging, 5.8 km walking, or 3.5 km for youth. The route leads from St. Anna Chapel through the forest south of Amerdingen, past historic sites such as the Celtic square enclosure and the Three Stones, as well as a small lake. Times are recorded via an app and transferred immediately to a leaderboard, making the event especially modern and accessible. The race is attracting increasing numbers of participants and offers a sporting challenge for all age groups.
course_highlights: Start at St. Anna Chapel
Forest course south of Amerdingen, with historic sights such as the Celtic square enclosure and the Three Stones
Route marked with directional arrows, with app-supported timekeeping
additional: The race is virtual and takes place in July, allowing participants to complete their runs at a time that suits them. Multiple entries and a second free attempt are possible. Results are recorded via an app and transferred immediately to the leaderboard. There are different course distances for different age groups and ability levels. Virtual race, route towards the Celtic square enclosure, online registration, event period from 01.07. to 27.07.2025, start times between 06:00 and 20:00, participation from age 8, donations to preserve the chapel

description: The Nordkirchen Half Marathon takes place on August 2, 2026, and offers a scenic course through Nordkirchen Castle Park and the Obsen farming community. Runners start at the stadium in Castle Park, complete two laps of the stadium, and then run a nearly 10-kilometer loop through picturesque parkland and villages. Several aid stations along the route provide refreshments for participants. The finish is back at the stadium, where spectators can cheer on the runners and enjoy a lovely time together.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the stadium in Nordkirchen Castle Park
Run through the expansive castle park with views of the castle
Loop through the Obsen farming community, where enthusiastic neighbors cheer runners on
additional: Personal refreshments can be dropped off before the start (8:00–8:45 a.m.). Water stations are located at km 4.5, 7, 9, 10.5, 14, 16.5, and 18.5. On-site late registration is available until 8:00 a.m. for an additional fee of EUR 3. Bibs with timing chips for electronic timekeeping will be issued and collected after the race, but participants may keep them as souvenirs. The course goes through Castle Park and Obsen, with the start and finish at the stadium in Castle Park. Registration is available online and on race day. Live results are available. Parking is available at the stadium, Nordkirchen Comprehensive School, and the Sundern car park.

name: 10. Charity-Lauf Koldingen
location: Koldingen, Pattensen, Region Hannover, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Koldingen Charity Run is part of the Sparkassen Running Pass of the Hanover Region, one of Germany’s largest running series, with 43 events in 2026. Runners can explore the Hanover Region on foot and collect stamps for their running pass at each event. The run offers a varied course in the beautiful surroundings of Pattensen and promotes recreational sport in the region. The event is open to everyone who wants to stay active while doing good.
course_highlights: Run through the scenic Hanover Region
Part of a major running series with 43 events in 2026
Opportunity to collect stamps for the Sparkassen Running Pass
additional: Participation in the Sparkassen Running Pass includes a digital app for collecting stamps and a digital running diary. A classic fold-out running pass is also available. The series features a variety of running events across the Hanover Region, with attractive rewards for taking part. The event offers laps for children and young people, with start times between 16:00 and 17:30, and usually takes place in August in warm weather.

name: 55. Volkslauf Rund um Wellen
description: The 55th Volkslauf Rund um Wellen takes place on August 2, 2026, in Beverstedt-Wellen and is one of Germany’s oldest marathon races, with a family-friendly atmosphere. The event offers challenging courses over four distances: marathon, half marathon, 11 km, and 5 km. Some courses are officially measured by the German Athletics Association (DLV). The routes pass through varied landscapes, including forest trails and different surfaces. The event is organized by TSV Wellen and relies on support from many local volunteers.
course_highlights: Marathon and half-marathon courses officially measured by the DLV
11 km course with varied surfaces and forest trails
Aid stations every five kilometers on the half-marathon and marathon courses
additional: Late entries are accepted until 30 minutes before the respective start, with a €3 late-entry fee (except for children’s races). Handwritten commemorative certificates are available for an additional €3. Changing rooms and showers are available at the start and finish area. Participants travelling from farther away can stay overnight in the sports hall by prior arrangement. First-aid services are provided by the German Red Cross. Course marshals are provided by the Wellen Volunteer Fire Brigade and TSV Wellen volunteers. Walkers are welcome in the 5 km, 11 km, and half-marathon events, but are not ranked separately. Multiple race distances, family-friendly, community event in a small village community, supported by the local volunteer fire brigade.

name: Hilpoltsteiner Burgfestlauf
description: The Hilpoltstein Castle Festival Run is a long-standing running event held as part of the Hilpoltstein Castle Festival, which takes place every year on the first Sunday in August. The event offers races for different age and ability groups, including Bambini, children’s, fun and main races. A special highlight is the Castle Hill Sprint in the main race, where the fastest runners can earn the title of Castle Hill King or Queen. The event is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and attractive course, with the start and finish on Marktstraße near the town hall.
course_highlights: 7.6 km main race with a Castle Hill Sprint after 500 metres
Course starts and finishes on Marktstraße near the town hall
Water available in the finish area and showers at the outdoor pool
additional: Race packs are distributed on event day from approximately 7:45 a.m. until 9:00 a.m. Safety pins are not provided. Parking areas around Hilpoltstein are signposted; the town centre is closed to traffic. Showers are available at the outdoor pool. Admission to the municipal swimming pool is free on event day upon presentation of the race number. Special award for the team with the most participants. Certificates are available by email or download. Prizes are awarded only to those present in person. The event includes distances from 0.6 km to 7.6 km; online registration is available. The start is at Siegertstraße 2. Families and children are a particular focus.

name: Kapellenlauf Vorra
location: DJK SC Vorra, Frensdorf, Bavaria, Germany
description: The Kapellenlauf Vorra is a traditional race organized annually by DJK SC Vorra. It offers several distances, including a half marathon, a quarter marathon over 10.55 km, and a fun run and Nordic walking, both newly added in 2025. The course runs through the rural surroundings of Abtsdorf and offers both competitive racing and a more leisurely run. The event also hosts the Upper Franconian Half Marathon Championships and attracts many participants from the region.
course_highlights: Half marathon and quarter marathon through the rural countryside
Course with two 5.5 km loops for the fun run and Nordic walking
Start and finish at the sports grounds in Abtsdorf
additional: The event patron starts the races promptly at 9 a.m. Nordic walking attracts a large number of participants and emphasizes enjoyment and community. The course is available to download as a GPX file. Changing facilities are available at the Beck restaurant. The event includes elevation gain and team classifications, with the start and finish at the Vorra sports grounds. Results and photos are available.

name: Olewiger Charity-Run
description: The Olewiger Charity Run in Trier is a diverse running event that combines sporting commitment with social solidarity. The event offers various races for all age groups, including a main race, youth race, children’s race and an inclusive race. 100% of all entry fees are donated to Demenzzentrum e.V. for the Trier region, underscoring the event’s charitable spirit. The races take place on August 2, 2026, offering a great opportunity to get active together for a good cause.
course_highlights: Volksbank Trier Eifel 5,000-meter main race
Optik Ruschel 1,000-meter youth race
dm-Markt 1,000-meter inclusive race
additional: The races have staggered start times: Bambini race at 10:25, inclusive race at 10:50, children’s race at 11:45 and main race at 12:15. The event is supported by regional sponsors who emphasize community spirit and the development of the Trier region. Several race categories are available, including a fun run, youth race, children’s race, inclusive race and elite race; registration opens in January 2026; the start is at the Volksfreund Torbogen and Volksbank Trier Eifel Torbogen; participants receive medals, goodie bags and drinks; parking and shuttle information is available.

name: XI Gorce Ultra-Trail
location: Ochotnica Dolna, Nowy Targ County, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: Gorce Ultra-Trail is a unique mountain race held in the picturesque area of Ochotnica Dolna. Participants can choose from five varied courses ranging from 5 to 102 km, suited to different experience levels, from beginners to seasoned ultramarathoners. The routes pass through the beautiful Gorce Mountains, featuring challenging climbs and spectacular views. The time limit for the longest course is 20 hours, underscoring the challenge and character of the event.
course_highlights: Five courses ranging from 5 to 102 km
Routes pass through the picturesque Gorce Mountains
20-hour time limit on the longest course, GUT 102
additional: Registration is online via time-sport.pl. Discount codes may be available to podium finishers from previous editions, residents of the Ochotnica Dolna municipality, and seniors. Refunds, distance changes, and transfer of race packages are governed by the regulations. Invoices can be requested during registration or by email. The time limit for the longest course is 20 hours. The event takes place in the summer, with registration open and details available about the regulations, logistics, and courses.

name: Kresowe Trail #9
description: Kresowe Trail is a small-scale trail-running event organized by the Kresowe Maratony Foundation, promoting a healthy lifestyle and respect for nature. The event in Narewka offers two running distances: Szpurt (7 km) and Wertep (16.6 km), along scenic routes with course markings and an aid station. Participants can expect electronic timing, commemorative medals, and a hot post-race meal. The event emphasizes ecology and the local community, creating a welcoming atmosphere for runners of all ages.
course_highlights: Szpurt course – 7 km, marked with green arrows on a yellow background
Wertep course – 16.6 km, marked with red arrows
Aid station on the Wertep course and careful course marking
additional: Online registration closes 3 days before the event. Registration is available on race day from 8:30, although the race package may be incomplete (for example, it may not include a medal). The time limit is 2 hours 15 minutes. Littering is strictly prohibited; gel and bar wrappers may be left in the aid-station area. The package includes a hot post-race meal with a vegetarian option, electronic timing, medical coverage, an aid station at the finish and on the Wertep course, points toward the series’ overall standings, and a special photography service. The event is scheduled for August 2, 2026, with previous results and archives available on the website. Participants can choose from different distances, and the event is very popular with the local community.

description: Panewnicki Bieg Dzika is a recreational running and Nordic Walking event held in the picturesque Panewnickie forests in Katowice. The event promotes an active, healthy lifestyle and the charms of the local natural environment. The approximately 4.9 km course is marked every kilometre and can be completed up to four times, within a time limit of 3 hours. The event is open to recreational participants and athletes affiliated with sports clubs. Participants can also learn about proper conduct in the forest.
course_highlights: Approximately 4,882 m loop through the Panewnickie forests
Course marked every 1 km
The loop can be completed up to 4 times, within a 3-hour time limit
additional: The time limit for completing the course is 3 hours. The course is marked every 1 km. Participants can run or walk the loop up to 4 times. Those born in 1950 or earlier are exempt from the entry fee. Entry fees can be paid by bank transfer to the KS AZS AWF Katowice account. A package covering all starts during the year is available for purchase. The event is recreational and educational in nature and promotes proper conduct in forest areas. Online registration; 3-hour time limit; running and Nordic Walking events; Panewnickie forest setting; race preparation and training plans.

name: Beh 2 míle Bratislava – 8. kolo
description: The Bratislava 2 Mile Run is a regular running race organized by the Sri Chinmoy Marathon Team at the Kuchajda swimming pool complex in Bratislava. The race covers 2 miles (3.218 km), with categories for children, juniors, women, men, and veterans. Registration takes place on site from 9:30, and the race starts at 10:00. The event is part of a race series in which runners earn points toward a perpetual trophy based on their performances and participation in individual rounds.
course_highlights: A 2-mile (3.218 km) course
Registration and start by the volleyball court at the Kuchajda complex
Categories for children, juniors, women, men, and veterans
additional: Registration takes place on site by the volleyball court from 9:30. The competition is for the Sri Chinmoy Marathon Team Perpetual Trophy, with points awarded based on performances and participation. In the event of a tie on points, the best time decides, followed by shoe size. Children have a separate category with a shorter course of approximately 200 m. The race takes place on a public road in Kuchajda; registration is also available on site, and the start is scheduled for 10:00. The event also includes a children’s category with shorter distances.

description: The Malý Kavečianský Marathon is a running event in Kavečany near Košice, offering 21 km and 7 km routes, as well as children’s races. The race starts at the football stadium and is open to a wide range of categories, from children to veterans. It is organized by TJ Mladosť Kavečany together with the Košice-Kavečany Municipal District. The event is suitable for runners of different ages and ability levels, with affordable entry fees and online registration available.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the football stadium in Kavečany
21 km and 7 km routes suitable for different age groups
Children’s races start at 9:10
additional: Women over 60 and men over 70 can enter for free. Categories include children’s, pupils’, youth, overall, and age-group categories for men and women. Children’s races start at 9:10. The route includes town streets and the football stadium; online registration is open until 1.8.2025; all categories start at 9:00.
